edition.locus: Gebhardt VII.VII (Dinocrates in the dark place)

source_text: Post dies paucos, dum uniuersi oramus, subito media oratione profecta est mihi uox et nominaui Dinocraten. Et obstipui quod numquam mihi in mentem uenisset nisi tunc, et dolui commemorata casus eius. Et cognoui me statim dignam esse et pro eo petere debere, et coepi de ipso orationem facere multum et ingemiscere ad dominum. Continuo ipsa nocte ostensum est mihi hoc. Uideo Dinocraten exeuntem de loco tenebroso, ubi et complures erant aestuantes et sitientes ualde, sordido cultu et colore pallido; et uulnus in facie eius, quod cum moreretur habuit. Hic Dinocrates fuerat frater meus carnalis, annorum septem, qui per infirmitatem facie cancerata male obiit, ita ut mors eius odio fuerit omnibus hominibus. Pro hoc ergo orationem feceram; et inter me et illum grande erat diastema, ita ut uterque ad inuicem accedere non possemus. Erat deinde in illo loco ubi Dinocrates erat piscina plena aqua, altiorem marginem habens quam erat statura pueri; et extendebat se Dinocrates quasi bibiturus. Ego dolebam quod et piscina illa aquam habebat, et tamen propter altitudinem marginis bibiturus non esset. Et experrecta sum, et cognoui fratrem meum laborare; sed fidebam me profuturam labori eius et orabam pro eo omnibus diebus quousque transiuimus in carcerem castrensem; munere enim castrensi eramus pugnaturi: natale tunc Getae Caesaris. Et feci pro illo orationem die et nocte gemens et lacrimans, ut mihi donaretur.
pass_a_gloss: After a few days, while we were all praying, suddenly in the middle of prayer a voice came forth to me and I named Dinocrates. And I was stunned because he had never come into my mind except then, and I grieved having recalled his fate. And I knew at once that I was worthy and ought to ask for him, and I began to make much prayer concerning him and to groan to the Lord. Immediately that very night this was shown to me. I see Dinocrates coming out from a dark place, where also there were many others burning with heat and thirsting greatly, with filthy clothing and pale color; and a sore on his face, which he had when he was dying. This Dinocrates had been my fleshly brother, seven years old, who through illness with his face eaten by cancer died badly, so that his death was hateful to all people. For him therefore I had made prayer; and between me and him there was a great interval, so that neither could approach to the other. Then in that place where Dinocrates was there was a pool full of water, having a rim higher than was the stature of the boy; and Dinocrates stretched himself up as if about to drink. I grieved that although that pool held water, yet because of the height of the rim he would not be about to drink. And I awoke, and I knew that my brother was in distress; but I trusted that I would help his distress and I prayed for him on all days until we passed over into the military prison; for we were about to fight in a military show: it was then the birthday of Geta Caesar. And I made prayer for him day and night groaning and weeping, that it might be granted to me.
pass_b_english: A few days afterward, while we were all at prayer, suddenly in the middle of prayer a voice came to me and I spoke the name Dinocrates. I was startled, for he had never entered my mind except at that moment, and I sorrowed when I remembered his fate. At once I knew that I was counted worthy and ought to intercede for him, and I began to pray long for him and to groan to the Lord. That very night this was shown to me. I see Dinocrates coming out of a shadowed place, where many others also were parched with heat and fiercely thirsty, mean in dress and pale in color, and on his face the sore that he had when he died. This Dinocrates had been my brother by blood, seven years old, who died wretchedly when disease consumed his face with a cancer, so that his death was abhorrent to everyone.

So I had prayed for him, yet between him and me a great gap stood, so that neither of us could reach the other (cf. Luke 16:26). Then, in the place where Dinocrates was, there was a pool full of water, whose rim rose higher than the boy was tall, and Dinocrates stretched upward as though to drink. I grieved because, though the pool held water, the height of the rim kept him from drinking. Then I awoke, and I knew my brother was suffering, but I trusted that I could aid his suffering, and I prayed for him every day until we were transferred to the camp prison, for we were to fight in the military games on the birthday of Geta Caesar. And I prayed for him day and night with groaning and tears, that he might be granted to me.

lemmas.gloss: to burn with heat, suffer heat

choices.why: diastema is a Greek loanword for an interval or space; rendered as physical gap because it blocks mutual approach in the vision.
munus here is a public spectacle, and castrense specifies the camp setting before the birthday games; not a gift or duty.

choices.english: that he might be granted to me
choices.why: passive donaretur with mihi as recipient; the object is Dinocrates' relief, asked of the Lord as a gift.
rejected: that it might be forgiven me
